record.title: Lithuania prohibits non-exempt foreign entry during the first pandemic wave
record.scope: Nationality/residency-based admission prohibition at land and rail frontiers
record.crossings: All Lithuanian land admission routes; Saločiai–Grenstalė documented in first-day field reporting; designated road and rail posts remained available for exceptions
record.exceptions: Residents, international transport crews, diplomats, NATO personnel and families, authorised entrants and controlled return transit; goods movement exempt.
record.imposing_authority: Lithuanian Government; State Border Guard Service
record.enforcement: BNS’s correspondent at Saločiai observed two foreign travellers turned back after midnight while returning Lithuanians proceeded. Reuters also interviewed a Latvian traveller crossing into Lithuania on 15 May.
record.consequences: Travellers outside admission exceptions were refused; no nationwide refusal total estimated.
record.relationship: Separate imposing authority and movement category from neighbouring-country restrictions. Reciprocal policies must not be added as extra border-wide days.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status inference at 21 October 2026
record.context: The quarantine package also limited routes and citizen departure. This record measures foreign entry; those overlapping restrictions need separate phase reconstruction.
record.uncertainty: The May endpoint is permission for Baltic citizens and lawful residents only. June permission and other-category rules continued separately. Exact first-day hour follows the official 00:00 wording; no continuous total-border closure inferred. The initial controls on 14 March are not coded as the foreign-entry prohibition onset. Fresh Reuters field reporting corroborates actual Baltic-category road passage at the May endpoint.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. No claim of a continuous nationwide operational closure.
